_readme: Deployment catalog. CONFIG, NOT CODE — adding a provider, model, or region
The split: a WIRE FORMAT is a request/response shape and needs a Python
implementation. There are only four, and new ones appear rarely. A
DEPLOYMENT is a (provider, endpoint, model, region, credential) tuple and
there are unboundedly many. Everything in that second category lives here.
This file carries NO SECRETS and is committed deliberately: publishing the
exact deployment matrix is part of the methodology. Credentials stay in
the environment (.env locally, Vault/SSM/Secrets Manager elsewhere) and are
models: an explicit list, or "auto" to take the most recently updated
models declaring both capabilities from the pinned models.dev snapshot.
LOCAL RUNTIMES: entries with "enabled": false are templates. Flip to true
once you have confirmed the port from the app's own settings — ports below
are the documented defaults, not verified on this machine. Run
`python3 run.py discover` to see what is actually listening.

wire_formats._note: Implemented in conformance/adapters/. Listed here for reference only.

deepseek.note: Advertises OpenAI compatibility. Whether that extends to enforcement is the open question.

ollama-native.note: Same weights as 'ollama', different wire. Controlled adapter experiment for P3.

lmstudio.note: LM Studio local server. Default port 1234; confirm in Developer > Local Server.

msty.note: Msty Studio local service. PORT UNVERIFIED — check Msty's local API settings and correct base_url before enabling.

llamacpp.note: llama.cpp llama-server. Thin OpenAI shim — a good adversarial test of compatibility claims.

vllm.note: vLLM OpenAI server. The realistic on-prem/air-gapped enterprise target.
